q: Why does SQL pull ahead in p99 only as write share grows?
a: Constraint checks make each write cost more, so write-heavy mixes compound the gap while read-heavy mixes hide it.

q: What question do you ask before picking?
a: The read:write ratio: p99 follows whatever class exceeds 1% of traffic, so pure reads narrow the gap to 15 vs 10.
Into the application: joins and transactions become N+1 reads and sagas you now own.
